The clinical images confirm a localized area of diffuse erythema, edema, and warmth on the left leg with indistinct borders, consistent with cellulitis. Given the newborn's elevated white blood cell count with neutrophilia and these physical findings, do you have any history of recent umbilical cord stump infection or trauma to that specific limb?

REQUEST TEST: C-Reactive Protein (CRP) and Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR).

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: C-Reactive Protein (CRP): 18.5 mg/L (Elevated), Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR): 45 mm/hr (Elevated)

speaker: Doctor
text:
The clinical picture of diffuse erythema, edema, and warmth on the left leg, combined with leukocytosis, neutrophilia, and elevated inflammatory markers (CRP and ESR), strongly supports a diagnosis of bacterial cellulitis in the newborn. Has the baby been exposed to any broken skin, such as a scratch or insect bite, on that leg?

REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis and Gram Stain of lesion exudate.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis: Negative for leukocytes, nitrites, or bacteria. Gram Stain of lesion exudate: Moderate quantity of Gram-positive cocci in clusters; no organisms seen in urine.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The Gram stain finding of Gram-positive cocci in clusters from the lesion exudate confirms a Staphylococcus aureus infection, which aligns with the clinical presentation of cellulitis.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Cellulitis (Staphylococcus aureus)
